'''Shabnam Akhtari''' is a Canadian-Iranian{{r|science}} mathematician specializing in [[number theory]], and in particular in [[Diophantine equation]]s, [[Thue equation]]s, and the [[geometry of numbers]]. She is a professor of mathematics at [[Pennsylvania State University]].{{r|psu}}

==Education and career==
Akhtari graduated from the [[Sharif University of Technology]], in [[Tehran]], in 2002 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in mathematics.{{r|shortbio}} She earned a [[Master of Science]] degree from [[Simon Fraser University]] in 2004, before continuing her graduate work in mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]], completing her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] there in 2008. Her dissertation, ''Thue Equations and Related Topics'', was supervised by Mike Bennett.{{r|shortbio|mg}}

She was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Queen's University at Kingston]] in Canada, the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in Germany and the [[Centre de Recherches Mathématiques]] in Canada before joining the [[University of Oregon]] faculty as an assistant professor of mathematics in 2012.{{r|shortbio}} She was tenured as an associate professor there in 2018.{{r|michler}}

==Recognition==
Akhtari is the 2021–2022 winner of the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].{{r|michler}}
